_doc: Revert-verify mutants for vault-exodev ems__Bug 290965dd: sameTerm compares RDF terms, a query constant included (SPARQL 1.1 §17.4.1.8, RDF 1.1 literal term equality). Each mutant removes one guarantee and must redden exactly the axes in `expect` (pairwise distinct within the spec). `red_re` anchors on the jest failure header `● <suite> › <axis> ` (ITRV §A44/§A104). Anchors are CODE lines only. `tree`/`subject` are placeholders — run the matrix on a copy with the paths substituted (§A145). Subject: the sameterm handler, sameTermArgument and constantTerm — a query constant reaches sameTerm as its exact term, DATATYPE(…) as the IRI it names, and a constant the engine cannot build is only the identical constant. `if (!node.datatype) return undefined;` is locked by F10 (spec review W1: the async evaluator's untyped node must keep the old path, T23).
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/core/src/infrastructure/sparql/filters/FunctionRegistry.ts

F1_left_constant_as_value._note: The LEFT argument is evaluated to its JS value again — no exact constant term, no IRI for DATATYPE(…). Red: every axis whose distinguishing constant (or IRI constant, or substituted value, or unbuildable constant) is on the LEFT.

F2_right_constant_as_value._note: The RIGHT argument is evaluated to its JS value again (same technique as F1). Red: most axes put the distinguishing constant on the right.

F3_lexical_from_value._note: The constant's lexical form rebuilt from its parsed JS value (4.20 → "4.2", "042" → "42"). Red: T5, T6 (4.20 / "042"), T16 ("0"^^xsd:boolean), T14 (NaN, which a JSON clone into EXISTS turns into null), T27 (""^^xsd:boolean becomes the buildable "false") and T31 (Infinity, the same JSON clone).

F4_language_ignored._note: The language tag is dropped: "x"@en and "x"@fr become one term. Red: T7 and T15.
F4_language_ignored.from: if (node.language) return new Literal(lexical, undefined, node.language);
F4_language_ignored.to: if (node.language === "\u0000") return new Literal(lexical, undefined, node.language);

F7_language_after_datatype_guard._note: The first prototype's order: the datatype guard before the language check drops a language-tagged value substituted into EXISTS (language, no datatype) to the old path, where its tag is lost.
F7_language_after_datatype_guard.from:
if (node.language) return new Literal(lexical, undefined, node.language);
    if (!node.datatype) return undefined;
F7_language_after_datatype_guard.to:
if (!node.datatype) return undefined;
    if (node.language) return new Literal(lexical, undefined, node.language);

F9_iri_constant_as_string._note: An IRI constant takes the old path (its string) — the plan's first draft, review HIGH. Red: T17, T21; T26 (xsd:string against DATATYPE(…), now an IRI); T27 (<tag:…> is then a string, not an unbuildable constant); T30 (the strings of STR(DATATYPE(…)) and CONCAT(…) meet the IRI constant, which is now a string too).

F10_untyped_node_as_simple_literal._note: Spec review W1: a literal node without a datatype becomes a simple literal of its text instead of keeping the old path. Such a node comes from the async evaluator's wrapper of a computed argument (EXISTS in an argument, ems__Bug 67c8925f) — and also from a simple literal substituted into EXISTS and a BIND string, where the old path is the same term for any non-empty string; the empty string is not (the engine's Literal cannot hold it) — no axis covers that: IF(EXISTS …, 42, 0) would equal "42", and an unbound value would become the literal "undefined". Red: T23.

F11_datatype_result_as_string._note: Spec review H1: DATATYPE(…) reaches sameTerm as the IRI's string, which is now a simple literal — sameTerm(DATATYPE(?x), xsd:integer) is always false (the base answered it right, both sides were strings). Red: T26, and T30 (DATATYPE(?l) equals STR(DATATYPE(?l)) again).

F12_unbuildable_as_old_path._note: Spec review M1: a constant the engine cannot build falls back to its JS value (the plan's prototype), which sameTerm now takes for a literal — "Asset Two"^^<tag:…> equals the stored label, a VALUES string equals <tag:…>, ""^^xsd:boolean equals false. Red: T20 (""^^xsd:integer twice: NaN !== NaN), T27, T29 (""@en and ""@fr are both "").

F13_empty_string_unbuildable._note: The empty simple literal is taken for an unbuildable constant too — STR("") no longer meets "". Red: T9.

F14_unbuildable_key_ignored._note: Any two unbuildable constants are one term. Red: T20 ("x"^^<tag:dt> vs "y"^^<tag:dt>, <tag:a> vs <tag:b>), T28 (""^^xsd:integer vs ""^^xsd:boolean), T29 (""@en vs ""@fr).
F14_unbuildable_key_ignored.from: return term1 instanceof UnbuildableConstant && term2 instanceof UnbuildableConstant && term1.key === term2.key;
F14_unbuildable_key_ignored.to: return term1 instanceof UnbuildableConstant && term2 instanceof UnbuildableConstant && term1.key !== "\u0000";

F19_datatype_by_value_prefix._note: Spec review round 2 V5: any computed string that looks like a W3C IRI is taken for an IRI — STR(DATATYPE(?n)) equals xsd:integer, a CONCAT of the text equals xsd:string. Red: T30.

F20_key_without_named_node._note: Declared zero (§A135): the unbuildable key drops its IRI flag. Defensive by construction — an IRI key has no datatype and no language, while an unbuildable literal always carries one of them (a node without a datatype never reaches the catch), so the flag never decides alone.
